thread:
IncidentBot: [PAGER] SEV-2 — Metering: token-count window drift and delayed reporting. A subset of requests are being double-counted for ~30-90s windows; customers are getting transient overage flags. Pager: #incidents. Link: https://redwood/pager/1759876543 :rotating_light:

Jules (oncall-sre): grabbing this. Can anyone confirm customer-facing symptoms?

Ivan (support): multiple support tickets inbound, mostly around sudden overage emails and invoices showing spikes. One enterprise account (txn-corp) flagged usage >3x for 01:15–01:17 UTC.

Riya (billing-ops): saw alerts from reconciler: job metering-recon reported delta > 20% for the 1m window rolling at 01:15. Also stacktrace in reconciler logs referencing window_epoch rounding.

Tom (eng-runtime): interesting — we pushed a change to aggregator windowing two deploys ago to make it align with tenant-sharded clocks. Could this be a rounding edge-case with seq_len batching?

Maya (eng-sre): quick status: redis-backlog of kv-cache was stable, but aggregator pods CPU spiked at 01:14 and GC pauses went from ~10ms to 120ms. Could explain delayed flush + retry counts.

Jules (oncall-sre): commands I'll run now:
```
# check aggregator rollout
kubectl -n metering get pods -l app=aggregator -o wide
kubectl -n metering logs deploy/aggregator -c aggregator --since=15m | grep -E "window|round|count"
```

Sam (billing-eng): paste of relevant log snippet:
```
2026-02-12T01:15:02Z aggregator INFO window_epoch=1707671700 computed_epoch=1707671701 delta_ms=1012 tenant=txn-corp tokens=12450
2026-02-12T01:15:02Z aggregator WARN rounding_mismatch tenant=txn-corp prev_epoch=1707671699
```

Leah (product-ops): customers care about two things: (1) transient overage emails, (2) invoices — we need to triage which customers saw billable increments vs. just UI/alerts.

Riya (billing-ops): running quick query to see impacted customers (this will be slow):
```
SELECT tenant_id, SUM(tokens) as tokens, window_ts
FROM billing.edges
WHERE window_ts BETWEEN '2026-02-12T01:14:00Z' AND '2026-02-12T01:18:00Z'
GROUP BY tenant_id, window_ts
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Ivan (support): flagging txn-corp, med-analytics, and openai-proxy as having support tickets. Will queue a proactive msg to txn-corp if spike is real.

Jules (oncall-sre): hypothesis: aggregator rounding + GC pause caused some in-flight batches to be re-emitted into the same window and the reconciler double-counted them. Short-term mitigation: enable strict de-duplication and route reconciler to ignore small out-of-order timestamps for 5m window.

Tom (eng-runtime): I can patch aggregator to add idempotency keys and stricter window-boundary checks. Quick patch ready, want to canary one pod.

Maya (eng-sre): please canary; also increase reconciler tolerance to 2s while we validate. Command to patch reconciler config on the fly: `curl -X PATCH https://config-api/configs/metering-reconciler -d '{"window_tolerance_ms":2000}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG'`

Sam (billing-eng): created a hotfix PR to add idempotency: PR #4321. If we roll that out, we should also run a backfill job to dedupe sucked tokens.

Jules (oncall-sre): executing canary restart of aggregator-1 now.

OpsRunbookBot: runbook referenced: https://runbooks/redwood/metering-windowing. Steps: 1) canary patch aggregator 2) increase reconciler tolerance 3) monitor DeltaCounts, 4) communicate to customers.

(1m later) Maya (eng-sre): canary pod started. CPU normalized and GC pause back to baseline. Initial metrics show delta counts dropping to within 1.8% for the last 2 minutes.

Riya (billing-ops): reconciler tolerance bumped to 2000ms. Running live recon: `python scripts/recon_live.py --window 01:14-01:18 --dryrun` shows 12 tenants would have been deduped; tokens corrected -4.1% aggregate.

Leah (product-ops): draft message for affected customers (propose sends to only enterprise tenants with >5% delta):
"Hi — we observed transient billing spikes for a subset of customers between 01:14–01:17 UTC due to an internal metering processing issue. We corrected counting and will reconcile invoices; no billing changes will be made without review. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with postmortem"

Ivan (support): ready to send to txn-corp and med-analytics once we confirm final numbers.

Tom (eng-runtime): canary looks good. I'm going to roll the patch across aggregator replicas with staged rollout (5% → 25% → 100%). Command: `kubectl -n metering rollout restart deployment/aggregator --image=aggregator:hotfix-4321`

Jules (oncall-sre): monitoring graphs: token-delta spike resolved, alerting silence configured for this incident window. Still watching for any stragglers.

(30m later) Riya (billing-ops): reconciliation finished. Summary: 27 tenants affected, median token drift +3.8% at peak, top-5 tenants listed. We'll hold any invoice changes and do manual credits if needed. Follow-up actions: manual reconcile run, audit logs, postmortem.

Leah (product-ops): customer comms approved. Ivan, please send to flagged customers with the drafted text + offer to review invoice lines.

Ivan (support): sent to txn-corp and med-analytics; they acknowledged and asked for estimated credit. Riya, can finance compute estimated credits?

Sam (billing-eng): I'll prepare reconciliation table and share invoice delta by tenant.

Jules (oncall-sre): incident is de-escalated to SEV-3; continuing monitoring. Owner for follow-up postmortem: Tom + Sam + Riya. Please add timelines and code pointers.

Tom (eng-runtime): note for postmortem: root cause likely combination of GC pause + window rounding edge-case in aggregator. Fix: idempotency keys + deterministic boundary calc.

Maya (eng-sre): I'll schedule a short runbook update to include steps for increasing reconciler tolerance and a playbook for quick canaries.

Leah (product-ops): thanks all. Closing notes: customers notified, hotfix rolled, reconciler backfilled. Postmortem assigned and due EOD tomorrow.

IncidentBot: Incident 1759876543 status updated to: mitigated -> monitoring. Close when postmortem created. :white_check_mark:
